candidate.title: CPT-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina overview of contiguity-preserving transposition sequencing (CPT-seq/CPT-Seq), specifically indexed Tn5 transposition in 96 reactions, EDTA stopping and pooling, dilution and redistribution into 96 physical compartments, SDS release, and compartment-indexed PCR to DNA libraries. Upper and lower rows illustrate independent compartments within one workflow, not alternative assays; exemplar states stand for the stated 96-way collections. The graph ends at the depicted DNA products. Readout interpretation is supported by Amini et al. full text, without extending the graph to unshown post-PCR pooling, sequencing, or computational steps.

states.label: Amplified combinatorially indexed DNA library: upper compartment
features: PCR products carry genomic inserts, the first-tier transposition code, and the second-tier physical-compartment code.
Each tier is a bipartite left/right code in the paper: the four index sequences plus genomic inserts can be read in the sequencing workflow.
A unique transposition/PCR code pair identifies a virtual compartment; 96 × 96 yields 9216 virtual compartments.

These short DNA products represent neighboring genomic elements from original long molecules. Shared indices support genomic read islands and phasing, rather than making every read in a compartment originate from one molecule.
The same code combination can contain multiple genomic islands; neighboring islands need not share a haplotype. Dilution reduces parental-copy collisions without ensuring perfect separation.

The drawn endpoint is DNA after PCR, not a directly sequenced intact long molecule or an already assembled haplotype. Sequencing and inference explain its intended use but are not additional depicted operations.

All material endpoints and 29 routes agree on attachment, first-index retention and new-well identity; the three joint split/mix operations are justified and separate processing is not collapsed under shared captions. Both SDS corrections are grounded in primary text and implemented by their surrounding interfaces. The DNA carrier, bipartite index readout, virtual-compartment interpretation and limitations are supported. CPT-seq is the only target and has a verified full-text paper association; all four other listed references are assessed at their actual evidence levels. No consequential unsupported assertion, in-scope omission or unresolved architecture question remains. Routine full-protocol additions and unshown post-PCR pooling/sequencing need not be added to the graph.

evidence.locator: [b00012] Results: independent first-round reactions
evidence.quote: As a concrete example, a single genomic sample is split in to M=96 independent transposition reactions, each employing unique indexed transposon adapters.

evidence.locator: [b00012] Results: pooling and physical redistribution
evidence.quote: These 96 separately indexed/adapterized genomic libraries (contiguity preserved), are then pooled, diluted, and redistributed into a set of N=96 discrete physical compartments (wells on a plate), with each physical compartment now having M=96virtual partitions.

evidence.locator: [b00013] Results: compartment-specific SDS and indexed PCR
evidence.quote: After physical compartmentalization, the DNA-transpososome complexes are denatured by addition of SDS detergent, and the content of each compartment is amplified with a pair of indexed PCR primers (96 different PCR indexes).

evidence.locator: [b00014] Results: genomic inserts and four index sequences
evidence.quote: After PCR, combinatorially-indexed libraries from all wells are combined and sequenced using a dual indexing workflow to read all four indexes (two bipartite codes each consisting of left and right indices) and genomic DNA inserts (Supplementary Fig. 3).
